narrative.overview:
Tessra’s visual world is an Operate surface inside a VS Code Webview: a precise local API instrument that disappears into Method → URL → Send → edit → inspect. It is not a marketing dashboard, not a SaaS console, and not a clone of stock VS Code chrome. Identity lives in method color discipline, dense editor rhythm, and quiet local-first cues — never in pill walls, nested cards, glow, or bounce.

The current request panel is an anti-reference. Redesign replaces that visual grammar entirely while preserving every functional contract. Theme presets remain as color/token variation only on one shared layout. Claims stay within PRODUCT.md.
keyCharacteristics: Strongest hierarchy always: Method → URL → Send → Request editing → Response
One quiet status strip for meta; success primary only in the response summary
Conditional response-first split after Send; request remains instantly editable
VS Code theme tokens + restrained accent; flat surfaces, thin dividers, compact toolbars
Compact editor density; progressive disclosure for defaults, variables, compare/mode
Tessra identity via method colors and quiet local cues — not dashboard spectacle

rules.name: The One Success Owner Rule
rules.body: Success green has a single primary owner: the response sticky summary. Send stays action-blue (or Connect equivalent). Meta chips never compete as co-primary status.

rules.name: The Host Token Rule
rules.body: Prefer VS Code CSS variables over hard-coded greys. Tessra-specific hex is reserved for method spectrum and a minimal semantic set that must remain legible across themes.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Do not use dashboard orthography (VARIABLE USAGE, wide letter-spacing, uppercase section theater). Prefer quiet labels: Env, Vars, Defaults, or inline contextual hints.

rules.name: The Primary Path Rule
rules.body: Meta (env, variable usage, default headers, compare, mode, profile) must never visually outrank Method → URL → Send → Request editing → Response.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: If removing a border, shadow, background, or radius does not hurt interaction or understanding, remove it.

dos: Do keep Method → URL → Send → Request editing → Response as the permanent visual hierarchy.
Do use one status strip with progressive disclosure for Environment, variable resolution, default headers, and preflight.
Do put success emphasis only on the response sticky summary.
Do keep a user-adjustable request/response split with persisted ratio; emphasize response after Send without trapping request edits.
Do render DEFAULT HEADERS as a one-line summary; keep header kv-rows primary.
Do treat theme presets as token/color skins on one structure.
Do preserve all functional contracts while replacing visual grammar.
Do prefer VS Code tokens, thin dividers, compact density, and visible focus.
donts: Don't polish the old pill/chip/card grammar — it is anti-reference.
Don't ship border-radius: 999px pill spam, nested cards, big rounded rects, shadows, glows, bounce easings, or hover translateY lift on chrome.
Don't use dashboard uppercase kickers or decorative empty-state orbits.
Don't duplicate success green on Send, Live Response, and response summary.
Don't keep Compare / Mode / infrequent actions in primary chrome.
Don't invent four preset layouts or compromise the redesign to preserve old preset looks.
Don't add airy SaaS whitespace that fights scannable editor density.
Don't invent brand claims beyond PRODUCT.md (no fake testimonials, sync features, or cloud positioning).
